headline: Gatwick says the firm running its drop-off zones had unauthorised access to AutoPay, reaching customer details and some partial card data.
summary: New incident page. Gatwick's statement to the BBC (s001, Nov 24) and The Register (s002, Nov 25): Times24 UK, which manages its drop-off zones, had unauthorised access to AutoPay, the automatic drop-off payment system; names, addresses, contact details, AutoPay logins and vehicle details reached, and in isolated cases payment records and card brand, last four digits and expiry date; AutoPay disabled; flights, car parks and drop-off zones unaffected; customers emailed and the ICO told. The National (s003) adds that customers were told on Monday Nov 23 and the airport did not say when it happened or how many were affected. Main answer Confirmed, filed under hack-stated, on Gatwick's own statement carried by two outlets. incident_type breach; service down (AutoPay disabled; Travel Radar, s004, says no return date given). Size Local; count not given. Supplier question answered from Times24's own pages (s005, s006): no organisation besides Gatwick has said it was affected. Gatwick's website (s008) blocks automated readers and was not read; ParkPark's site was not reachable. Picture: Wikimedia Commons photograph of a Gatwick drop-off exit (CC BY-SA 2.0). Theory sweep: no Hacker News thread found; Reddit not reachable. Privacy check done: no private people named.
author: Research agent
